text:
deploy-bot: Release 2026.03.12-rc-8 -> prod blocked. Post-deploy healthcheck failed for web-frontend v2.1.3. Error: missing config key 'AUTH_JWT_SECRET' in prod. See /deploys/1966667000 for logs.

mike: wait — staging had a migration earlier today that renamed the key, right? how did staging pass?

eva: staging had an alias/compat mapping applied by the staging pipeline: it writes both paths. Prod pipeline didn't. We missed adding the alias to the prod KMS write step.

ben: so options are backfill prod KMS or rollback/pin to v2.1.2. Which is faster?

sara: Backfill is a small ops change but needs approval. Rolling back is trivial (pin image) but disruptive to release cadence. Thoughts?

ops-bot: Oncall: @mike (respond with :ack: to accept). Ticket created if needed.

mike: ack. I'd prefer to avoid full rollback if backfill is low risk. Who can apply the KMS alias?

eva: path mismatch: the new deploy expects /redwood/prod/web/auth/jwt; old path is /redwood/prod/web/auth/secret. Staging had an intermediate compat entry. Prod doesn't.

ben: that explains it. I suggest: 1) pin prod to v2.1.2 to stop further automatic promotion, 2) ops backfill compat alias, 3) re-run canary of v2.1.3, 4) update release notes and add preflight check.

mike: agree to plan. Devex, can you pin the image tag in helm/chart for the running deployment temporarily?

devex: I can do helm patch now. Running: `kubectl -n prod set image deploy/web-frontend web-frontend=ghcr.io/redwood/web-frontend:2.1.2` and `kubectl rollout pause deploy/web-frontend` after.

deploy-bot: Rollout status: canary=10% failed checks -> blocked. Manual action required.

ops-bot: Created INC-2345 to track KMS backfill; approvers: sara, mike.

sara: approving now. I'll run the backfill command: `kms write /redwood/prod/web/auth/jwt --value-from /redwood/prod/web/auth/secret --alias` (dry-run then apply). ETA ~12m.

ben: after backfill, we should add a release checklist bullet: verify secret key aliases exist and are consistent across envs. Also add a preflight deploy-bot hook that checks both key names.

eva: +1. Also include a short mapping in release notes: `AUTH_SECRET (legacy) -> AUTH_JWT_SECRET (new)` and which services are affected.

mike: ok. If backfill succeeds we'll unpin and promote. If anything else fails, we'll keep 2.1.2 and schedule a proper rollout after thorough validation.

devex: added release note draft: /docs/releases/2026-03-12.md and opened PR to add preflight check to deploy-bot.

sara: backfill complete. Verified both KMS paths present and service can read `AUTH_JWT_SECRET` via the prod env.

mike: unpausing canary and promoting to 30% now.

deploy-bot: Canary re-run: healthchecks passing at 10% -> 30% (observability p95 latency stable).

ben: monitoring for next 15m. If stable we'll scale the rest. Postmortem: short note about env parity gap — the alias only existed in staging pipeline.

eva: wrote the postmortem draft and linked the gap to the pipeline release step. Proposal: require symmetric KMS writes in CI for all environments.

mike: filing final postmortem ticket and tagging SLA review. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:

sara: quick follow-up: I'll add a one-liner to the release notes so customers see the secret key rename and that we performed a compatibility alias during rollout.

ben: nice. Closing thread when monitoring window is complete.
